subject: Taxes
title: Mental Accounting and Taxes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mental Accounting and Taxes.

hook.text: People treat money differently depending on where it comes from. A $1,000 bonus feels different from a $1.

buildup.text: Richard Thaler's mental accounting theory shows people sort money into invisible categories: salary, windfalls, savings.

discovery.text: Tax refunds are treated as 'bonus money'—spent more freely than salary.

twist.text: That refund is your own overpaid money returned without interest. Economically, you gave the government a free loan.

climax.text: Mental accounting makes people love tax refunds—the government's best trick. It turns overpayment into a celebration.

punchline.text: Your own money, returned late. But it feels like a gift. Mental accounting.

quiz.question: Why do people enjoy tax refunds even though it's their own overpaid money?
options: Because they earn interest on it
Mental accounting makes it feel like bonus money
The IRS pays a premium on refunds
